body: 飲食料品の消費税率を1％に引き下げる消費税減税の関連法案が11日、参議院・本会議で審議入りしました。このまますんなり決まるのか?街では早くも減税に向け、苦慮するところもあるようです。【図を見る】「支援金」の給付イメージ　政府案と公明党案の違いは?■財務省幹部いわく「政局カード」…支援金の対象はなぜ不明?井上貴博キャスター:国会の会期末は12月の中旬です。これから1か月間で、消費税減税をするのか・しないのか、するならばどのような形で行うのかを議論する必要があります。日本の行く末を占う、極めて重要な1か月となりそうです。消費税減税法案が参議院でも審議入りしました。これは、日々購入する飲み物や食べ物の消費税を8％から1％に下げるというものです。そして1％分を国民に給付しますが、その対象が明らかになっていません。なぜ、与党として明らかにしないのでしょうか。TBS報道局経済部 蓮井啓介 記者:減税法案と一緒に、支援金というものがあります。政府が支援金の対象者を明らかにしていない理由として、財務省幹部は「対象者と額は政局カード。野党の意見を聞いて決める」とコメントしています。つまり、少数与党のなかで野党の賛同を得るための交渉の切り札となるため、まだ対象を示していないというのが実情です。井上貴博キャスター:野党の出方をうかがいながら、どうしようか策を練っているという状況ですね。現在、参議院は自民党と日本維新の会の少数与党です。この2党だけでは法案を通すことができません。では、野党はどう出てくるのか。ポイントは、与党が公明党と国民民主党を取り込めるかどうかで、これが1か月間の非常に重要な分かれ道になってきます。与党としては、どのような給付イメージを掲げているのでしょうか。支援金は、年収が約100万円から約350万円の国民を対象者にしようとしています。政府が掲げている案では、2000万人ほどが給付の対象になります。また、野党とのやり取りを踏まえ、高市総理は年収350万円より対象を拡大する意向も示しているということです。

title: 懸命に働くは美徳51% 読売調査
body:
読売新聞社は「働き方」についての全国世論調査（郵送方式）を実施した。一生懸命働くことを美徳だと「思う」は５１％と半数にとどまり、若い人ほど低かった。「思わない」は４７％だった。【写真】「ワークライフバランスという言葉を捨てます」
日本社会では長らく、真面目に働くことが美徳とされてきた。「思う」と答えた人を年代別でみると、６０歳以上は５８％だったのに対し、４０～５９歳は４７％と半数を割り、１８～３９歳では４３％だった。「思わない」は、１８～３９歳が５６％と最も高く、４０～５９歳で５１％、６０歳以上で４０％だった。
日本人は外国から勤勉と評価されてきた。日本人の勤勉さについて、これからも続くと「思う」は４５％にとどまり、「思わない」は５３％だった。「思う」は年代別で１８～３９歳が４３％、４０～５９歳が４２％、６０歳以上が４８％。すべての年代で５割を下回った。
ＡＩ（人工知能）は働く現場にも浸透しつつある。仕事でＡＩを「使っている」は２６％、「使っていない」は７２％だった。ＡＩの普及が人間の働き方に与える影響について「仕事の効率が上がる期待の方が大きい」は５７％だった一方、「人間の仕事が奪われる不安の方が大きい」は３８％で、不安を感じる人が一定数いることが明らかになった。
調査は８月２４日～９月３０日、全国の有権者３０００人を対象に行い、２０００人から回答を得た（回答率６７％）。

title: CEOの解任可否を決定へ NVIDIA
body: Alexandra Alper[１１日　ロイター] - ジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の２件の不倫問題に揺れる米半導体大手エヌビディアは１１日に取締役会を開き、同ＣＥＯ解任の可否を決定する。‌事情に詳しい関係筋がロイターに明らかにした。同社は取締役会に関するコメン⁠ト要請に応じていない。フアン氏が退任すれば、時価総額約４兆ドルの同社の経営トップに空白が生じることになる。同社は人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルの学習やオープンＡＩの「チャットＧＰＴ」な​どのサービス稼働に使う半導体で圧倒的なシェアを持ち、米中のＡＩ覇権争いの焦点となっている。６３歳のフアン氏は明確な後継者がおらず、エヌビディア株‌の約３．６％を保有し、同社に対する強固な支配を築いている。ＤＡダビッドソンのテクノロジー調査担当責任者ギル・ルリア氏は「エヌビディアには後継者計画がないため、フアン氏の即時解任は同‌社にとって難しい事態を招きかねない。‌フアン氏が法律や社内規定に違反したのであれば、取締役会は​証拠を得次第、行動する可能性が高い」と述べた。エヌビディア取締役会がフアンＣＥＯの解任に向けて準備を進めてい‌ると米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）が最初に報じたのを受け、エヌビディア株は時間外取引で約８％下落。フアン氏と中国人実‌業家女性との関係について取締役会​が調査を発表して以降、今週の時価総額の減少額は約６０００億ドルに達した。また、‌ニューヨーク・タイムズ（ＮＹＴ）は、フアン氏が直属の部下とも不倫関係にあったと報道。相手はヘルスケア担当バイスプ⁠レジデントのキンバリー・パウエル氏だと伝えた。ＮＹＴによると、１１日に電話取材を受け、パウエル氏との関係について問われたフアン氏は「私に直接話をすべきではないと思う」と述べ、その後電話を切った。エヌビディアとパウエル⁠氏はコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。ロイターはこの報道を直​ちに確認できなかった。中国人‌実業家女性のアリス・フアン氏はシンガポール企業メガスピードの元幹部で、中国政府のスパイだった疑いが持たれている。米情報機関は、アリス氏が中国企業へのエヌビディア製半導体の出荷を手助⁠けしてきたとしている。フアン氏は８日、従業員向けのメモで妻に不実な行為をしたことを認め、「⁠全責任」を負うと表明したが、その関係の詳細は明らかにしなかった。投資家やアナリストらは、エヌビディ⁠アのチップに対する需要が短期的には落ち込む可能性は低いものの、同社が支援する幅広い企業群は打撃を受ける可能性‌があると⁠指摘した。バンテージ・ポイント・アセット・マネジメント（シンガポール）のニック・​フェレス最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）は「エヌビディアは投資ブームに資金を供給している循環的な資金の中心にも位置している」と述べた。

title: EU「ダークパターン」禁止へ
body: 欧州連合（EU）の行政を担う欧州委員会は11日、オンライン上での不公正な商慣行を包括的に規制するデジタル公平性法（DFA）案を公表した。「ダークパターン」と呼ばれる、本来望まない選択に誘導する画面設計などを禁止し、デジタル経済社会の消費者保護をめざす。【深掘り】「ダークパターン」日本でも欧州委は発表で、人々がオンラインで買い物や契約ができる便利な時代になったが、「その便利さは公正さの犠牲をともなってはならない」と指摘。消費者保護だけでなく企業の成長のためにも新たな規制が必要だと指摘した。法案は、不公正な手法を列挙して規制する。例えば、商品がほぼ売り切れであるかのような虚偽の表示で購入を迫ったり、手数料などを含む総額を決済直前まで表示しなかったりするダークパターンはリスト化して禁止する。イベントなどのチケット転売は元の合計価格などの明示を求める。■未成年向けゲームは有料ガチャも禁止インフルエンサーが企業からお金をもらってSNSなどで商品を紹介する際には「広告」の表示を義務化し、広告主の監督責任も明確にする。サブスク（定額制）のサービスは、無料期間の明示や自動更新前の情報提供が必要となる。ゲームなどでは、未成年者に対し、ギャンブル性のある有料ガチャや課金して有利になる機能の提供を禁止する。自動応答システムやAI（人工知能）の普及を念頭に、消費者は人間とコミュニケーションをとる権利を持つことも明記。商品購入を代行するAIエージェントを使う際にも事前に契約範囲や利益相反を確認するなど消費者の権利があるとした。

title: イベ閑散波紋 出演料まだ払われず
body: 鳥取県倉吉市で開かれたグルメイベントを巡り、SNSなどを通して全国に波紋が広がっています。一体なぜこれほどの事態に陥ったのでしょうか?出店者、そしてステージイベント出演者に話を聞きました。【写真を見る】“集客5万人”掲げた食フェスが炎上　ステージイベントで「ステージ未設営」　アスファルトで熱唱した出演者は…「イベントとしては終わってた」　出演料は未だ支払われず事の発端は、先週末、鳥取県倉吉市で開かれた大型グルメイベント『ローカルフードファイトin鳥取』。倉吉市で週末に開催された「ローカルフードファイトin鳥取」。県内外から多くの飲食店が集結する大型グルメイベント、当初「集客5万人」を謳っていたといいますが、会場は閑散としていたといいます。出店した業者は「集客5万人と聞いて出店したが実際は500〜1000人程度。食材は相当余ってしまいました。県外の方の出店も多く、前泊の旅費・宿泊費、食材費、かなり痛手だったと思います。」集客不足だけでなく、テントや電気、洗い場など会場準備も不十分で、イベントは混乱したまま幕を下ろしたといいます。また、イベント直後、主催側のHPやSNSが閲覧できなくなるなど連絡が取りづらい状態となり、出店者たちの不信感と怒りが爆発。インターネットを中心に大きな議論を呼び、今や全国的な関心を集める事態へと発展しています。大阪から参加した出店業者「もう早期に見切りをつけて、2日目のお昼過ぎには撤収したんですけど。肌感で1000人は来てないですね」こう話すのは、大阪から参加した出店業者。トラブルは、イベント当日を迎える前から始まっていました。事前に「テントや水道、テーブルや椅子は運営側が用意する」と案内があり、「前日の午前10時から搬入可能」と説明されていました。しかし…大阪から参加した出店業者「前日の夕方頃に着いたんですけど、テントも何も立ってない状態で。あと、冷蔵冷凍車ですね。前日に現地に来ていて、そこに搬入して保管・保存できるということだったんですけど、来てなかったですね。」食材などを無駄にしてしまったという出店者も多く、現場は混乱。さらに、のしかかったのは金銭的負担です。

title: スペイン 14年ぶりの全国ゼネスト
body: [マドリード １１日 ロイター] - スペインで１１日、住宅の高騰と家賃負担の深刻化に抗議するゼネストが実施され、労働組合は約４００万人が参加したと発表した。今月２９日に予定される総選挙‌を前に、住宅問題への不満が大規模な抗議行動として表面化した。全国規模のゼ⁠ネストは、ユーロ圏債務危機下で緊縮財政に反対して行われた２０１２年以来１４年ぶり。スペインの主要労組、労働総同盟（ＵＧＴ）と労働者委員会（ＣＣＯＯ）が主導し、家賃上昇や立ち退きに反発する借家人​団体も加わった。サンチェス首相は政権中枢を巡る汚職問題や先月発生した列車事故から世論の関心を逸らそうという動機から、あえて住宅問題を巡る有権者の‌不満を争点化したい考えだ。ただ世論調査では与党・社会労働党の支持率は依然として野党を下回っている。スト参加は地域によって差があったものの、住宅不足や家賃上昇が深刻な沿岸‌部で特に強い支持が見られた。首都マドリード中‌心部のグランビア通りでは、プリマーク、Ｈ＆Ｍ、プル＆ベアなどの店舗が​シャッターを下ろし、デモ参加者が気勢を上げて警官隊が厳重な警備に当たった。バルセロナでも多数の店舗が‌休業し、騒乱に備えて板で窓を覆う店もあった。スペイン銀行（中央銀行）によると、同国の住宅不足は約７５万戸に達しており、２０２８年までに１００万戸を超える‌見通し。住宅購入が難しくなる中で賃貸​需要が急増し、平均家賃は月額１１７６ユーロ（約１３１５ドル）と、若年層の平均月収の９８．７％に相‌当する。マドリード在住で病院のＩＴ部門に勤務するヘスス・ゴンサレスさん（３６）は「家賃も住宅価格も上がり続けており、一人⁠暮らしは不可能だ」と訴えた。経営者団体ＣＥＯＥのデミゲル副会長は、住宅不足による採用難で企業も被害を受けていると指摘。「ゼネストは問題解決につながらない」と批判しながらも、住宅建設の拡大や関連税の引き下げが必要だと主⁠張した。労組によると、港湾や自動車産業では参加率が９０％に達し、フォルク​スワーゲンのナバラ工場や同社‌傘下のセアトのバルセロナ工場では操業が全面停止した。送電事業者レッド・エレクトリカによると、午前１０時から１１時にかけて電力需要は最大１５．５％減少した。バルセロナ地下鉄は通勤時間帯以外の運休を発表。マドリード地⁠下鉄ではラッシュ時の利用者数が前週同時間帯比で４２％減少した。ただＢＢＶＡリサーチのチーフエコノミス⁠ト、ミゲル・カルドソ氏は、在宅勤務の普及やサービス業比率の上昇により、経済への打撃は過去のストより限⁠定的になるとの見方を示した。具体的には国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）を年間で０．１－０．２％押し下げる可能性があるとしている。警察によると、ストに関連‌して事務⁠所や工業団地の封鎖、ごみ容器への放火など４７６件の事案が発生し、正午までに４０人を逮捕した。労組​側は催涙ガスや警棒を使用した警察の対応でデモ参加者２０人が負傷したとして、「過剰な対応」だったと非難し、刑事告発する方針を示した。

title: 露ウ 大規模な捕虜交換で合意
body: ロシアによるウクライナ侵略の終結に向けた米露ウクライナ3カ国の高官協議は11日、アラブ首長国連邦（UAE）の首都アブダビで2日間の日程を終えた。露代表団のメジンスキー大統領補佐官は11日、協議終了後に記者会見し、露ウクライナが大規模な捕虜交換で合意したと発表した。ロシアの占領下にあるウクライナ領の扱いなど重要問題で進展があったかどうかは明言しなかった。一方、ウィットコフ米和平交渉担当特使とともに協議に参加したトランプ米大統領の娘婿クシュナー氏は協議後、ウィットコフ氏と露首都モスクワを12日に訪問してプーチン露大統領と会談し、アブダビでの協議の結果について話し合うと明らかにした。露国営タス通信が伝えた。（小野田雄一）

title: メーガン妃の父親 保釈中に再拘束
body: イギリスのヘンリー王子の妻、メーガン妃の父親が、足首に装着された電子監視装置を取り外した疑いで、アメリカで再び拘束されました。【画像】父親が児童ポルノ所持で逮捕されたメーガン妃メーガン妃の父親、トーマス・マークル容疑者（82）は、6日、子どもの性的虐待画像などを所持した疑いでFBI（連邦捜査局）に逮捕され、その後、足首への電子監視装置の装着などを条件に保釈されていました。しかし、イギリスの公共放送BBCによりますと、マークル容疑者は10日足首の監視装置を取り外した疑いで、フロリダ州で再び拘束されました。裁判官は保釈を認めず、拘置するよう命じたということです。マークル容疑者をめぐっては、カリフォルニア州ロサンゼルス近郊の貸倉庫2カ所から、子どもへの性的虐待画像などおよそ80点の証拠品が押収されています。マークル容疑者は逮捕前画像の所持を否定していました。

title: 米財務長官 脅迫受け軍基地に転居
body: David Lawder　Kanishka Singh[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] - ベセント米財務長官がイランから殺害の脅迫を受け、最近、首都ワシントンの自宅から米軍基地に転‌居した。事情に詳しい関係者２人が１０日明らかにした。米紙ニューヨーク・タ⁠イムズが最初に報じた。ロイターが１０月下旬に確認したメモによると、トランプ政権の情報機関高官は、米政府関係者や米国民を狙うイランの計​画がかなり進展していると警告していた。ベセント氏は８月以降、イランに船舶への攻撃停止とホルムズ海峡の再開放を迫るため、「‌オペレーション・エコノミック・アウトキャスト」と名付けた米国の制裁・経済圧力作戦を主導している。海上輸送の要衝である同海峡は、米‌国とイスラエルが２月２８日にイランを攻撃‌して以来、ほぼ閉鎖された状態が続いている。経済圧力作​戦は米海軍によるイランの港湾封鎖と並行して実施されており、イランとの取引を支‌援する中東の銀行支店やその他の金融サービス会社への制裁が含まれる。米財務省の報道官は電子メールで寄せ‌た声明で「長官はイラン政権の​脅迫にひるむことなく、オペレーション・エコノミック・‌アウトキャストの遂行と封鎖の維持に引き続き全力を尽くす。両措置が相まってイラン経⁠済を崩壊させつつある」と表明した。ニューヨーク・タイムズは、ベセント氏への脅迫がどの程度深刻なのかは現時点では不明だと報じた。事情に詳しい関係者によると、米紙ウォール・⁠ストリート・ジャーナルがベセント氏のジョージタウ​ン地区の邸宅を上空か‌ら撮影した写真を掲載したことで、同氏の身辺警護を巡る懸念が強まった。ベセント氏は２０２５年１月に財務長官への就任が承認された直後、この邸宅を１２５０万ドルで購入していた。同関係⁠者は、写真から自宅の所在地を特定できるようになったため、安全⁠確保に向けてベセント氏を軍基地に移したと説明。「公職者への脅威が高まる中、報道機関に⁠は責任ある行動を取る義務がある」と述べた。イランはこれまで、米国内で当局者や一般市民への攻撃‌を計画し⁠ているとの疑惑を否定している。ニューヨーク・タイムズによると、米当局​者は、イランが米国をはじめとする国外で大規模な攻撃を実行する能力は限られていると指摘している。

title: 約6300の学校に爆破予告メール 伊
body: イタリアでは11日、およそ6300の学校に爆破予告のメールが届き、生徒らが一時避難するなど、混乱が広がりました。メローニ首相は、「危険性はない」としたうえで、政府内で会議を開き、事態の把握を進めるとしています。【画像】英テレビ局　「安全上の脅威」を受けたと発表　数時間前にはアイルランドの放送局に爆破予告…ヨーロッパ各地で脅迫相次ぐ同様の爆破予告は、イギリスの数百の学校にも届き、一部で避難措置がとられました。ヨーロッパでは先週、旅客機やテレビ局に対する爆破予告も相次いでいました。

title: CEOの解任可否を決定へ NVIDIA
body: Alexandra Alper[１１日　ロイター] - ジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の２件の不倫問題に揺れる米半導体大手エヌビディアは１１日に取締役会を開き、同ＣＥＯ解任の可否を決定する。‌事情に詳しい関係筋がロイターに明らかにした。同社は取締役会に関するコメン⁠ト要請に応じていない。フアン氏が退任すれば、時価総額約４兆ドルの同社の経営トップに空白が生じることになる。同社は人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルの学習やオープンＡＩの「チャットＧＰＴ」な​どのサービス稼働に使う半導体で圧倒的なシェアを持ち、米中のＡＩ覇権争いの焦点となっている。６３歳のフアン氏は明確な後継者がおらず、エヌビディア株‌の約３．６％を保有し、同社に対する強固な支配を築いている。ＤＡダビッドソンのテクノロジー調査担当責任者ギル・ルリア氏は「エヌビディアには後継者計画がないため、フアン氏の即時解任は同‌社にとって難しい事態を招きかねない。‌フアン氏が法律や社内規定に違反したのであれば、取締役会は​証拠を得次第、行動する可能性が高い」と述べた。エヌビディア取締役会がフアンＣＥＯの解任に向けて準備を進めてい‌ると米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）が最初に報じたのを受け、エヌビディア株は時間外取引で約８％下落。フアン氏と中国人実‌業家女性との関係について取締役会​が調査を発表して以降、今週の時価総額の減少額は約６０００億ドルに達した。また、‌ニューヨーク・タイムズ（ＮＹＴ）は、フアン氏が直属の部下とも不倫関係にあったと報道。相手はヘルスケア担当バイスプ⁠レジデントのキンバリー・パウエル氏だと伝えた。ＮＹＴによると、１１日に電話取材を受け、パウエル氏との関係について問われたフアン氏は「私に直接話をすべきではないと思う」と述べ、その後電話を切った。エヌビディアとパウエル⁠氏はコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。ロイターはこの報道を直​ちに確認できなかった。中国人‌実業家女性のアリス・フアン氏はシンガポール企業メガスピードの元幹部で、中国政府のスパイだった疑いが持たれている。米情報機関は、アリス氏が中国企業へのエヌビディア製半導体の出荷を手助⁠けしてきたとしている。フアン氏は８日、従業員向けのメモで妻に不実な行為をしたことを認め、「⁠全責任」を負うと表明したが、その関係の詳細は明らかにしなかった。投資家やアナリストらは、エヌビディ⁠アのチップに対する需要が短期的には落ち込む可能性は低いものの、同社が支援する幅広い企業群は打撃を受ける可能性‌があると⁠指摘した。バンテージ・ポイント・アセット・マネジメント（シンガポール）のニック・​フェレス最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）は「エヌビディアは投資ブームに資金を供給している循環的な資金の中心にも位置している」と述べた。

title: CEO去就巡る報道 NVIDIA株下落
body: （CNN）　米半導体大手エヌビディアの株価が、11日の時間外取引で急落した。同社のジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（CEO）が社内の幹部と不適切な関係にあったという報道に加え、取締役会がフアン氏の去就について協議するために会合を開いていると報じられたことを受けたものだ。【画像】スパイ疑惑の渦中にいる女性と行動を共にするフアンCEO、計3枚米東部時間午後6時時点で、エヌビディアの株価は8.4%下落した。世界で2番目に時価総額が大きい企業である同社の株価は、米紙ニューヨーク・タイムズがフアン氏と幹部との不適切な関係を報じたことをきっかけに下落した。さらに米紙ウォールストリート・ジャーナルが、フアン氏解任の準備を取締役会が進めていると報じたことで下落に拍車がかかった。同氏は30年前にエヌビディアを共同設立した。今回の新たな報道に関してエヌビディアにコメントを求めたが、現時点で回答は得られていない。この数日前、エヌビディアの取締役会はフアン氏が「外国の諜報（ちょうほう）活動の標的」となっていたかどうかを調査すると発表していた。これに先駆け、フアン氏については前出の幹部とは別の女性と関係を持っていたという報道が浮上。米当局者はその女性を中国のスパイだと見ている。フアン氏は8日に不適切な関係があったことを認めて謝罪したが、相手の氏名は明らかにしていない。取締役会がフアン氏の解任を決定した場合でも、同氏の後継者となるべき明確な「ナンバー2」は存在しない。フアン氏自身、以前に「後継者計画（サクセッション・プランニング）」という考え方には懐疑的だと述べている。人工知能（AI）ブームの中心にあるこの半導体メーカーについて、投資家たちはフアン氏がトップの地位から追われた場合の先行きを懸念している。フアン氏は、AIの最も熱心な推進者かつ出資者の一人であり、投資家たちは同氏の描くハイテク業界隆盛のビジョンに惹（ひ）かれてエヌビディア株に殺到してきた。週末にフアン氏が自身の不倫を認め、さらにエヌビディアの取締役会が調査に乗り出したというニュースが伝わると、同社の株価は9日から10日にかけて9.5%下落した。エヌビディア株の下落はより広範な市場にも波及し、11日午後6時30分時点で、ナスダック100先物は1.1%、S&P 500先物は0.5%それぞれ下落した。

title: Amazon出品者「安値強要された」
body:
国内最大規模の通販サイトを運営するアマゾンジャパンに対し、公正取引委員会が１１日、独占禁止法の「確約手続き」を適用した。独禁法上の問題が指摘されたのは、多くのサイト利用者が商品購入の参考にする「おすすめ出品」の仕組みだった。【図解】アマゾンストアの「商品表示の仕組み」
「実質的に安い価格での販売を強要されていた」。「楽天市場」など複数サイトで生活用品を販売する大阪府内の男性会社役員（５４）はアマゾン側の対応をこう振り返る。
公取委によると、同社が運営する「アマゾンストア」では同じ商品だとしても、他サイトと同価格以下で配送条件などが良い商品を抽出し、「おすすめ出品」として優先的に表示する仕組みを設けている。おすすめ出品以外は別のページでしか掲載されず、購入手続きに進むボタンもすぐに表示されないため、出品者にとっては死活問題だ。売り上げを確保するため、中には赤字での販売を余儀なくされた出品者もいた。
アマゾンは２０１９年９月からこうした仕組みを始め、出品者に他サイトの最安値を通知し、この価格以下に設定するよう事実上誘導していた。公取委幹部は「アマゾンは自社でコストを負わずに出品者に負担を強いて、他サイトとの競争力を維持していた。他サイトが企業努力で価格を割安にしても、労せずに低価格で販売できる仕組みだった」と指摘する。
確約手続きは独禁法に基づく行政処分で、事業者は法令違反の認定と排除措置命令などの強制的な処分は免れる一方、違反疑いがある行為の解消に向けた改善計画を提出する。
今回、公取委が認定した同社の計画によると、同社は来年５月までに現在の仕組みを改善。おすすめ出品以外の表示枠を新設し、ストア内で最安値の商品についても消費者に分かりやすくする。出品業者の一人は「価格の決定権が販売者にあるという、本来のマーケットになってほしい」と期待を込めた。
こうしたアマゾンの価格管理の手法は、海外当局も問題視している。

title: Amazon「表示枠」公取なぜ問題視
body: ネット通販大手アマゾンが、同社の通販サイトの運営をめぐる問題を調べていた公正取引委員会に改善策を提出した。アマゾン通販サイトこう変わる調査の焦点となっていたのが、優先的に商品を表示する「カートボックス」という枠だ。どんな仕組みで、何が問題だったのか。アマゾンの通販サイトでは、同一商品を複数の業者が出品しているケースがある。サイト内では、1事業者の出品だけが優先的に表示される。その表示枠が「カートボックス」だ。「今すぐ買う」「カートに入れる」のボタン表示もあり、そのまま購入手続きに進める。一方、それ以外の出品は、「他の出品者」の表示をクリックしなければ目に触れることがない。表示の差が大きかった。サイト内で購入された商品の大半はカートボックス経由だったという。他の通販サイトにも、特定の出品者を検索画面の上位に表示する枠はある。しかし、他の出品者の商品も一覧で表示されるため、アマゾンほど差は出にくい。■問題視したアマゾン独自の選定条件公取委が問題視したのが、アマゾンがカートボックスに選ぶ条件と、それが出品者に与える影響だ。アマゾンは出品者に、カートボックスの条件として、他の通販サイト以下の価格を求めていた。これが独占禁止法上、不当な値下げ強要に当たる疑いがあるとみていた。アマゾンが提出した改善計画のポイントは、カートボックスの条件を満たす出品がひとつもない商品では、サイト内で最安値の出品者を目立つ表示にすること。これまでは、他のサイト以下の価格の出品がなくカートボックスが作られない場合、すべての出品が目立たない表示になり、消費者に気づかれないおそれもあった。（長妻昭明）

title: なぜ ブラックフライデーが長期化
body:
11月27日の「ブラックフライデー」を前に、セールの早期化が1か月規模に広がっています。
アカチャンホンポは前年の4週間から5週間に延長。ドン・キホーテは一部店舗での先行企画を含め最大31日間、ニトリは26日間にわたり実施します。イオンもネット限定先行セールを前年の9日間から16日間に拡大しました。
クリスマスや年末年始の商戦を控える中、なぜブラックフライデーのセールはこれほど長くなっているか考えます。
秋冬の注目セールは「ブラックフライデー」がトップ出典：Vポイントマーケティング株式会社　2026/10/2(金)
ブラックフライデーなどセールへの期待が高まる一方､ 物価高や節約意識も影響し､11月の消費意欲指数は前年並みに出典：生活総研　2026/10/30(金)
消費者の約半数（47%）は、物価や金利、雇用の先行きといった経済状況が、今年のホリデーシーズンの買い物計画にマイナス出典：Shopify Japan 株式会社　2026/10/7(水)
発祥の米国でもブラックフライデーは1日限りではなく、2026年はウォルマートが11月から12月初旬にかけて複数回のセールを設け、アマゾンも12日間開催します。そのため日本特有の現象ではありません。
長期化には複数の背景があります。イオンは先行セールを延ばす理由として、注文・配送の集中を分散させる狙いを説明。一方、Gapは11月の購入者に12月1〜25日に使える50％OFFカードを配り、次の買い物につなげています。
12月にはクリスマスや年末のセール、年明けには初売りが控えています。ブラックフライデーを前倒しすれば、秋から年始にかけて販売機会が連続することになります。
企業側には顧客との接点を保つ利点がある一方、セールの名称が変わっても値下げの対象や条件は同じとは限りません。消費者は「いつまで安いか」ではなく、「何が、いつ、いくらになるか」を見比べることが重要です。そのためセールの早期化が進むことで、かえって“買い時”を見失う“買い時迷子”という新たな消費者心理も生まれています。
皆さんは、ブラックフライデー、年末セール、初売りのうち、どのタイミングで買い物をしますか？

title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
summary: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
body:
Watch: Protesters and police clash in Barcelona
Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas.
Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.
Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.
The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant."
There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields.
Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city.
Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store.
The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful".  She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there."
She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets.  "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said.
Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads.
The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.
Police said they had made dozens of arrests
"We've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets."
Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable".
The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later.
Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460.
That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions.
Watch: Protesters gather across Spain for first general strike in 14 years
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform.
Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes.
And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing.
"Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes.
Tyres were set on fire in the city of Gijon in northern Spain
The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain.
PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election.
Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike."
Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid.
Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights.
The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC.
Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment.
He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills.
"It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas."
He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible."
With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible".
Gonzalo Álvarez, who was taking part in the general strike, says 50% of his salary goes towards rent
However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing.
"This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said.
Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election.
Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector.
Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%.

title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
summary: Colom is the first black person from the southern state elected to the US Senate in over 140 years.
body:
Why Democrat Scott Colom’s Senate win in Mississippi is so significant
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.
Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years.
Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.
The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called.
Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS.
Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well.
"While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said.
Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced.
The room burst into deafening applause and cheers.
"This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board.
"This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising.
"This is a historic election."
Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory.
"When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy."
Colom supporters celebrate his win in Jackson, Mississippi
The result wipes away a Republican winning streak in the Magnolia State that dates back to 1982.
The contest was never expected to be this close, with Hyde-Smith running for re-election in a state that President Donald Trump won in the 2024 election by more than 22 points.
But Democrats have scored a series of major wins in these midterm elections, taking control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate.
The party flipped Senate seats in Republican strongholds, including Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa.
Polls suggest this was due in large part to voter frustrations with the economy and the Iran war under President Trump.
Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith has been in the Senate since 2018
Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans.
Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls.
Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices".
The Democrat campaigned aggressively, visiting all of Mississippi's 82 counties.
Hyde-Smith's campaign assailed Colom as a puppet of billionaire liberal donor George Soros, whose family has helped fund the Democrat's political campaigns.
The 67-year-old Republican was criticised for a lack of public appearances.

title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
summary: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
body:
On Thursday Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Moscow and Dublin to hold talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents
Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day.
Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion.
However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon.
Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest."
"I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible.
Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said.
After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.
The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe.
For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member.
For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion.
Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system.
That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence.
Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.
Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them.
Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.
Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday.
Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin.
There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted.
Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added.
Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are essential to its security.
Moscow, meanwhile, has never backed down from its demand that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds. "Every inch" of land would be "returned to Russia one way or another", Medinsky said.
Kushner acknowledged that the territorial question remained the hardest, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region.
Later, Budanov admitted the talks had been "tough" and that Ukraine's priority was to ensure Russia could not attack it again.
"These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this."

title: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
summary: The news comes at a turbulent time for Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.
body:
Gibran Rakabuming Raka has been mired in a growing controversy over his high school credentials
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, an aide has told the BBC, in a move which could further strain the political alliance that helped propel President Prabowo Subianto to power.
It comes after Indonesia's Supreme Court ruled that a high-school document used during Gibran's 2024 election campaign was invalid.
The ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.
The aide, Budi Arie, said Gibran's resignation letter was submitted directly to Prabowo on Wednesday. It remains unclear if it has been accepted.
Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office.
Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials.
Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated.
"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said.
It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion.
Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school.
On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said.
Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.
Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40.
His resignation comes as tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared.
Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.
In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.
Last week, authorities arrested presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation - on suspicions of wiretapping the president.
Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi.
Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration.
All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The  free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.
On Tuesday, students across the country staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

title: Some under-25s should get less benefits, Milburn review to say
summary: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
body:
Alan Milburn will publish his review next week
Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.
Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits,the Times reported,external.
Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet".
He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.
His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element ofuniversal creditorpersonal independence payment(Pip).
Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit.
Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions.
But many claimants would receive less under the plans, which the government is set to take forward into legislation in the new year.
Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers.
Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate.
Speaking to the Times about his report, Milburn said: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.
"But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances.
"I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around."
Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year.
Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare reform under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.
The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence.
If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings.
The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch," Milburn added.
He said that currently "you've got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job".
His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, where young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options.
"A deal isn't a deal unless there are potential consequences," Milburn said. "Entitlements and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin."
A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work.
"But the prime minister has been clear that we need a wholesale change in the way we support young people to grow up in this country, where we invest in their success rather than paying for failure."

title: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
summary: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
body:
Poundland looks set to avoid immediate collapse after its US owners told MPs on Wednesday they were in favour of extending a deadline to find a rescue deal.
The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by Gordon Borthers from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation told the BBC they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release funding in recent days.
A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal.
Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.
The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims.
But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.
The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further £9m from Poundland's accounts, on top of £10m announced earlier. This will grant the company an additional 10 days to find a new buyer.
There are three bids currently on the table for Poundland, all of which have so far been rejected by the Gordon Brothers, who stand to profit from selling the company and its stock piecemeal.
Following the meeting between MPs on the business and trade committee and representatives of Gordon Brothers, chairman Liam Byrne told the BBC he was "deeply concerned" and described the firm's behaviour as "much like a wolf on Wall Street, on the British High Street".
"They refused to prioritise, protecting jobs and stores over and above their own financial returns," he added.
"It's clear that they've taken millions out of Poundland at a time when they themselves said the business was on a knife edge."
Byrne said the committee's message to Gordon Brothers was to ensure Poundland had "access to the funds that it needs to trade at what should be one of the busiest periods in the year".
He urged Gordon Brothers to "do what is right to save jobs and stores and do that now".
"It's a good business, it's a much-loved business, and particularly in the middle of the cost of living crisis, communities up and down the country rely on access to the kind of stores that it operates," Byrne added.
Following the private meeting with MPs, Poundland's chief executive Barry Williams told the BBC the chain's board would hold an urgent meeting on Wednesday night.
Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners.
Poundland boss Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget.
He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m.
However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".
It has argued the best way of securing jobs may be to split up the business and sell chunks of its 600 sites to other retailers.
There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up.
The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain.

title: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
summary: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
body:
Traditional games, squishies and building sets are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show.
The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK.
The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana.
The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10.
Despite relatively low sales in recent years, the toy sector has been buoyed by sales to "kidults".
The kidult market - which is toys and games for those aged over 12 - has been growing, particularly as adults buy toys for themselves.
This growth has continued with a 22% increase in the value of sales in the first half of the year.
But Melissa Symonds, UK toys director at Circana, said that toys for children - which still represents the majority of sales - had recorded a good year so far.
Growing public debate around children's screen time and the role of technology meant squishy toys, stickers and building sets such as Lego were popular.
"Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing that traditional, hands-on play remains overwhelmingly popular," she said.
Concerns have been raised about the suitability of some connected devices.
ABBC investigation foundan AI teddy marketed as being "perfect" for children as young as three said "I can't help with killing you" after seemingly mishearing a question.
Meanwhile, debate has intensified about keeping youngstersfree from smartphones during the school day.
One in five parents of children aged three to nine say the chance to play together as a family influences what they buy, according to market intelligence company The Insights Family.
Paul Reader, who chairs the Dream Toys selection panel of retailers and experts across the sector, said that parents wanted to engage with their children's play.
"Nothing beats a board game with that. Nothing beats a bit of interaction," he said.
The panel he chairs has selected a list of toys that retailers believe will be some of the most popular this year.
It includes variations on popular toys of recent years, including slime, a soft tiger that roars and grows, and a shark that breaks out of an egg.
Symonds said that, despite rising sales in the year so far, nearly half of toy sales came in the build-up to Christmas, and families were still looking closely at costs.
There was significant growth in toys priced between £5 and £10, she said.
Reader also urged anyone looking for a bargain to shop around, but to ensure that toys were bought from reputable traders so they were genuine and safe.

title: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
summary: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
body:
If production is approved, oil and gas will be pumped up through a large ship 80 miles north west of Shetland
Some Labour MPs have called on the government to reject the Rosebank oil field, saying it is "incompatible" with the UK's climate commitments.
There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland will be given the go-ahead.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that a decision would be "taken in due course" while Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh stressed thataffordability of energy billswas her "overriding objective".
But in a sign of the division within the party, more than a dozen Labour MPs expressed concerns in Parliament about approving it. Others expressed support, pointing to economic benefits.
Supportive Labour MPs said some other parts of the world emitted far more greenhouse gases than the UK and warned of relying on imports. Reports have suggested that Chancellor John Healey is in favour of approval.
Separately, it is understood some Labour backbenchers have organised a letter opposing Rosebank - intended for Burnham, but not yet sent - which more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs have indicated they support.
One signatory told the BBC that approving Rosebank "would not create new jobs, would bring minimal money into the Treasury and be bad for the climate".
"The government's central aim is to tackle the cost of living crisis, and drilling for more oil at Rosebank isn't the answer," the MP said.
Wednesday's Westminster Hall - a type of parliamentary debate where backbench MPs raise topical issues but do not vote - was organised by Green MP Carla Denyer.
Labour MP for Sheffield Central Abtisam Mohamed told the debate: "Rosebank fails on every test.
"It will not benefit taxpayers who will shoulder the vast majority of the development costs, it will not strengthen our energy security because most of the oil will be sold on international markets, and it will not reduce energy bills for our constituents, who will remain exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices."
Richard Burgon, a former frontbencher on the left of the party, said: "Rosebank is not compatible with our climate targets - it's dangerous to pretend otherwise."
The UK is committed to reaching net zero by 2050 and wants to limit global warming to no more than 1.5C above the pre-industrial period.
The UK government has always insisted that Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision,formally resting with Fahnbulleh. She green-lit production in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea last month, but Rosebank hangs in the balance.
Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh will formally announce the Rosebank decision, expected in the coming weeks
Labour's manifesto upon entering power in 2024 pledged not to "issue new licences to explore new fields".
Licences for both Jackdaw and Rosebank were granted by the then Conservative UK government in 2022 and 2023 respectively.
But the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that the government had made the approvals unlawfully, leaving the current Labour government to make a fresh decision on whether to give the go-ahead.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenochsought to tease at Labour divisionson the issue during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday.
During the debate, Labour MP Anna Gelderd said: "We live in an unprecedented era where our energy security is more vital than ever, in which jobs and wealth must be protected and economic opportunities seized - on both of these points, Rosebank fails."
Labour MP Julia Buckley said she had received opposition to Rosebank from her constituents in "regularly flooded Shrewsbury" and said fossil fuels "belong in the past, not the future".
She urged Fahnbulleh to "reject the oil licence in favour of renewables", adding: "Please don't add further to our climate emergency."
Other Labour MPs expressed their support, including recently departed veterans minister Al Carns, who warned that Britain wouldcontinue to need fossil fuelsfor decades and importing more would be a mistake.
"Refusing to produce it here does nothing on its own to eliminate that demand - it simply increases our reliance on imports which can carry their own environmental cost," he added.
Those representing communities with ties to the oil and gas industry, including Jonathan Brash, the Labour MP for Hartlepool, stressed the benefits of approving Rosebank for British jobs.
Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, Labour MP Bill Esterson, chair of Energy Security and Net Zero Committee, said "the economics of it (Rosebank) are that you should carry on with it" and "there's an element of energy security" by approving it.
Energy minister Michael Shanks told the debate the government would take a "pragmatic approach" to a clean energy transition, stressing it was "not a turn off the taps government, but nor can we justifiably be a drill every last drop government either".
"This government will not make decisions for this country which are not compatible with our climate obligations," he added.

title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become the face of the US AI boom
Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.
Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation". The FBI is alsoconducting its own probe.
The company's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (£375bn) wiped of its stock market value since Friday.
Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, given it is the sole manufacturer of a computer chip used in AI tools.
It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials who are keen to win the AI race.
Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.
Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.
Nvidia has also maintained that the US government did not inform it that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington earlier this year warning that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Beijing has rejected claims that the Nvidia chief has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China".
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang, who had said he had "no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed him.
However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing.
The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before it, if deemed necessary.
When announcing on Sunday that itwould investigatethe affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce.
Joon Kim is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focusing on fraud and other criminal acts.
The Nvidia investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with the company.
He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity.
It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang.
A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI.

body:
Alan Milburn will publish his review next week
Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.
Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits,the Times reported,external.
Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet".
He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.
His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element ofuniversal creditorpersonal independence payment(Pip).
Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit.
Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions.
But many claimants would receive less under the plans, which the government is set to take forward into legislation in the new year.
Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers.
Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate.
Speaking to the Times about his report, Milburn said: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.
"But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances.
"I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around."
Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year.
Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare reform under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.
The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence.
If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings.
The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch," Milburn added.
He said that currently "you've got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job".
His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, where young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options.
"A deal isn't a deal unless there are potential consequences," Milburn said. "Entitlements and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin."
A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work.
"But the prime minister has been clear that we need a wholesale change in the way we support young people to grow up in this country, where we invest in their success rather than paying for failure."

title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive
summary: Thousands of messages seen by BBC show how a Chinese official sought details of sensitive political matters.
body:
Watch: Chris Cash says counter-terror officers entered his bedroom and arrested him
A British man who was charged with spying for China has told the BBC he was a "convenient fall guy" for UK police and security services who wanted to put espionage threats by foreign states "on the map".
Chris Cash, a former parliamentary researcher, has shared more than 6,000 messages with us revealing how a Chinese official sought information about sensitive political matters in the UK - including the 2022 Tory leadership battle to decide the next prime minister.
The messages show how Cash's friend in China, Chris Berry - with whom he had been sharing information - dramatically described a "secret" meeting between Berry and a high-ranking Chinese official.
Berry said he had been told that China was concerned about how a British MP it had sanctioned might be promoted to a cabinet role.
The messages also reveal how Cash used his friend as a reference during vetting for a parliamentary pass - which was approved.
Like Cash, Berry was also charged with espionage. The two men consistently maintained their innocence.
In Cash's first interview since his acquittal, which sparked a political row over the government's failure to designate China as a "threat", he says he would "never do anything" to harm UK national security.
But he admits he was "unprofessional and naive" to send "gossiping" texts to his friend, whom he met in 2018 when they both taught English in a school in China.
Although the trove of messages shows him discussing sensitive topics, there is no evidence in them that Cash was paid by, or sympathetic to, the Chinese Communist Party.
Chris Cash, left, and Chris Berry met in 2018 when they were teaching in China
With the government having previously said that Chinese spies were targeting UK officials across the political, defence and business sectors with increasingly sophisticated espionage operations, Cash believes his case was pursued as a warning to others.
Berry declined to comment on this story, but at the time of his acquittal said he denied any wrongdoing and that he had been "unfairly subjected to a trial by media".
He said he had provided reports to a Chinese company, which he believed had clients seeking to develop trading links with the UK, and those reports contained no classified information and relied on public sources.
Cash returned to the UK in 2019, saying in his resignation message for his job in China that he felt "guilty sitting back and participating in a system that I am uncomfortable with".
He later became the director of a small policy group run by China-sceptic Conservative MPs in Westminster.
Meanwhile, Berry stayed in China writing reports for a large consultancy which, like many Chinese companies, has links to the government.
Inside the China Spy Case
The espionage row that rocked Westminster
Watch:Inside the China Spy Case on the BBC News YouTube channel,external
UK security services alleged that information from the men's messages, sent on the encrypted messaging app Signal between January 2022 and March 2023, had been passed to people linked to the Chinese state.
England and Wales' top prosecutor said the case had collapsed last autumn because government officials could not say China had been classed as an "enemy" at the time.
This prompted accusations of UK political interference to placate the Chinese government.
China has previously called the allegations of spying "pure fabrication and malicious slander".
The most striking section of the messages handed to the BBC concerns Berry's account of his meeting in summer 2022 with a senior Chinese official who wanted to have "a more detailed co-operation".
In voice notes Berry describes how, beforehand, work colleagues had told him the official's interest had been piqued by reports Berry had written, which included details of the UK's foreign policy approach to China.
In the voice notes, Berry says he was initially aghast, but then decided: "I thought it would be interesting to go anyway… not really intending to do anything."
Listen: Berry tells Cash about his invitation to meet a senior Chinese official
Berry tells Cash he was driven to a government-owned villa in a grand compound.
The experience "felt like a psychological game of chess" and "like a test", Berry says.
He kept his hands under the table as tea was served: "I didn't want it to be obvious if I was nervous. I tested to see if my hands were shaking first, then drank the tea."
Berry describes the senior Chinese official asking via an interpreter "about the situation in the UK at the moment, about the Tory leadership thing".
At that time, Boris Johnson had just resigned as the UK's prime minister, and a Conservative leadership battle was taking place, which Liz Truss would go on to win.
Berry says he jokingly tried to ask his host which candidate China wanted, but the interpreter did not translate his question.
"And then the main guy just shakes my hand like it's time to go," Berry tells Cash.
After receiving the voice notes, Cash replies via text the next day: "You, my friend, have just been elite captured" before adding: "You're in spy territory now".
In many media reports these particular messages, previously released in a government witness statement, have been presented as a smoking gun - evidence that Cash knew his friend was passing on information to the Chinese state.
But Cash insists it was a "tongue-in-cheek joke" because he knew his friend to be "a staunch critic of the Chinese Communist Party".
The next morning, he made a joke about Berry spying for the UK and getting in trouble with the Chinese authorities, he says. Cash texted: "Keep him sweet… We may have a use for you yet".
"I didn't believe he was knowingly spying on the UK through me," says Cash. "I trusted my friend… I wish I had seen the danger earlier, spotted it and cut off all contact."
So who was the mystery official Berry had met?
"I found out who this guy is," Berry text-messaged Cash a few hours later. "Bigger deal than I thought."
Berry posted a link to the Wikipedia page of Cai Qi, who at the time was one of China's most influential politicians and is now, in effect, President Xi Jinping's chief of staff.
Berry identified Cai Qi (left) as the man he had met - a trusted aide of Chinese President Xi Jinping
Whether Berry correctly identified his host remains unclear. He has since disputed the suggestion that he met someone as senior as Cai Qi.
What is beyond dispute is that he believed he may have met someone highly placed within the Chinese political system.
For Chris Cash, this unusual encounter did not prompt alarm bells. Asked why not, Cash tells the BBC: "Because I didn't think anything of the meeting, really."
We ask Cash why his friend might have been asked to such a meeting. "Strange things happen in China... you know we would often brush shoulders with sort of quite senior members of the Chinese communist party," he tells us.
Challenged about whether he had read the Wikipedia link at the time, Cash says he had "skimmed it", adding that it described him as a judge and a provincial-level official. "I just thought it was a weird meeting with a guy who'd taken an interest," he says.
Six months later, Berry said in text messages that "off the record" he had it "on pretty good authority" that China was considering dropping sanctions against Tom Tugendhat, one of the Conservative MPs in the China Research Group, where Cash worked.
Berry wrote that this would happen as long as the West "continued to show signals that they are willing to work together".
The Chinese believed it would be "extremely embarrassing" if Tugendhat became prime minister or foreign secretary while under Chinese sanctions, Berry said.
At the time of the meeting in summer 2022, China-sceptic Tugendhat was seen as a possible contender to succeed Boris Johnson, or become UK foreign secretary.
He was actually appointed as security minister by Liz Truss, and Beijing lifted sanctions on him in January 2026.
Was Cash concerned that Berry appeared to be passing information to him about Chinese foreign policy?
Cash says he assumed Berry had heard this "through the grapevine at his company" which was doing business with the UK.
He says he never doubted his friend's trustworthiness, to the extent he even named Berry as a reference on his application for a security pass for the Palace of Westminster.
The pass was granted and, a fortnight before their arrests in early 2023, Cash invited Berry to Parliament for lunch.
It was to be their final face-to-face conversation.
Cash was in bed at quarter to six on a March morning when he was woken by car doors being shut, he says. Within seconds, four UK counter-terrorism officers had barged into his bedroom at his parents' home in Edinburgh.
"They told me to sit up and not touch anything and then said I was under arrest for breaching the Official Secrets Act," Cash says.
"I was in complete shock… quivering... My mum was hysterical."
Cash says the officers dressed him in dirty clothes he had worn that weekend, handcuffed him and marched him down to an unmarked police car. He was later driven to London.
Chris Berry was also arrested the same day.
It remains unclear how, when and why British security services became interested in the exchanges between the two friends.
But they are likely to have found out far more about their relationship when Berry was stopped and questioned by counter-terror officers at Heathrow Airport.
His laptop and phone were taken - this may have enabled his Signal chats to be downloaded.
Berry later messaged Cash about it.
Cash says he had not been alarmed by this: "I thought it was just standard... for a guy who'd been in China."
As the investigation progressed, it became clear the authorities believed Cash and Berry had been involved in an informal, but dangerous, exchange of information that was "prejudicial to the safety and interests of the UK".
The allegations were based on 6,27

title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census
summary: It comes after a Lib Dem MP said black English or Asian English should be specific options for respondents.
body:
Andy Burnham has signalled his support for dedicated options at the next census to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English.
It comes after Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde called for legislation to widen ethnicity options for respondents at the next population count, due in 2031.
The last census, held in 2021, saw English offered within a broader white category, but without specific options for black English or Asian English.
Asked at Prime Minister's Questions whether he would support Babarinde's proposal, Burnham said he had not seen details of the plan.
But he added: "I stand here thinking that I would want to support that bill, to directly take on the poisonous politics we've seen from some in this House".
"We must bring people back together. I am interested in working with anyone in this House who shares that aim," he added.
Burnham did not respond to a follow-up question from Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey about whether he would meet Babarinde to discuss his plan, and he did not specify whether the government would give it time for debate in Parliament.
Babarinde introduced his proposal for legislation on Tuesday, under a rule that allows MPs to propose new laws in a 10-minute speech.
Such draft laws, known as private members' bills, rarely become law without support from the government of the day but are often used by MPs to raise awareness of issues and generate media attention for policy ideas.
Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP
Respondents to the 2021 census were asked a two-stage question about ethnicity, with options grouped under five broad ethnic headings.
In Wales, the terms "Asian Welsh" and "Black Welsh" were listed in the broad categories themselves, and respondents were able to pick "Welsh" as an option underneath the broader white category.
The form in England listed "English" as an option in the white ethnic category, but the only way for respondents to describe themselves as Black English or Black English was via a free-form text box.
In Scotland, the term "Scottish Asian" appeared in the broad categories, whilst "Black Scottish" was given as an example response for the text box.
Speaking on Tuesday, Babarinde said his proposed law would introduce Black English and Asian English as specific new categories, arguing that the text box on the current form "may as well be the margin".
Babarinde's proposal has been backed by some MPs in other parties, including Labour former deputy prime minister David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly, who quit the shadow cabinet this summer to run for London mayor.
The Eastbourne MP has previously told the BBC he put forward his bill in the wake of comments by former Conservative home secretary Suella Braverman, whodefected to Reform UKearlier this year.
Bravermanwrote in 2015,externalthat she was British Asian but said she "cannot claim to be English" despite being born and educated in England.
She has reaffirmed her position in recent weeks, writing on X that Englishness was "an ethnicity" and it was "not racist to say this".
"To say I'm English is to take a 'laissez-faire, anything-goes' attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity. It also denies me my Asian heritage," she added.
The detailed questions asked during the census in England and Wales are set out in legislation following recommendations from the Office for National Statistics (ONS).
The ONS told the BBC that the Government Statistical Service has been working on a new approach to asking about ethnicity in official surveys since 2022, with an update on the work due to be published on Thursday.
That could lead to a recommendation to change the ethnicity question at the 2031 census, although the questionnaire itself is normally designed much closer to the time the census is due to take place.
Legislation setting out the questions for the last census was published in summer 2020, ahead of it taking place in March the following year.
The Scottish governmentdelayed the censusin Scotland until 2022 because of the Covid pandemic.

title: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
summary: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
body:
If production is approved, oil and gas will be pumped up through a large ship 80 miles north west of Shetland
Some Labour MPs have called on the government to reject the Rosebank oil field, saying it is "incompatible" with the UK's climate commitments.
There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland will be given the go-ahead.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that a decision would be "taken in due course" while Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh stressed thataffordability of energy billswas her "overriding objective".
But in a sign of the division within the party, more than a dozen Labour MPs expressed concerns in Parliament about approving it. Others expressed support, pointing to economic benefits.
Supportive Labour MPs said some other parts of the world emitted far more greenhouse gases than the UK and warned of relying on imports. Reports have suggested that Chancellor John Healey is in favour of approval.
Separately, it is understood some Labour backbenchers have organised a letter opposing Rosebank - intended for Burnham, but not yet sent - which more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs have indicated they support.
One signatory told the BBC that approving Rosebank "would not create new jobs, would bring minimal money into the Treasury and be bad for the climate".
"The government's central aim is to tackle the cost of living crisis, and drilling for more oil at Rosebank isn't the answer," the MP said.
Wednesday's Westminster Hall - a type of parliamentary debate where backbench MPs raise topical issues but do not vote - was organised by Green MP Carla Denyer.
Labour MP for Sheffield Central Abtisam Mohamed told the debate: "Rosebank fails on every test.
"It will not benefit taxpayers who will shoulder the vast majority of the development costs, it will not strengthen our energy security because most of the oil will be sold on international markets, and it will not reduce energy bills for our constituents, who will remain exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices."
Richard Burgon, a former frontbencher on the left of the party, said: "Rosebank is not compatible with our climate targets - it's dangerous to pretend otherwise."
The UK is committed to reaching net zero by 2050 and wants to limit global warming to no more than 1.5C above the pre-industrial period.
The UK government has always insisted that Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision,formally resting with Fahnbulleh. She green-lit production in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea last month, but Rosebank hangs in the balance.
Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh will formally announce the Rosebank decision, expected in the coming weeks
Labour's manifesto upon entering power in 2024 pledged not to "issue new licences to explore new fields".
Licences for both Jackdaw and Rosebank were granted by the then Conservative UK government in 2022 and 2023 respectively.
But the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that the government had made the approvals unlawfully, leaving the current Labour government to make a fresh decision on whether to give the go-ahead.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenochsought to tease at Labour divisionson the issue during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday.
During the debate, Labour MP Anna Gelderd said: "We live in an unprecedented era where our energy security is more vital than ever, in which jobs and wealth must be protected and economic opportunities seized - on both of these points, Rosebank fails."
Labour MP Julia Buckley said she had received opposition to Rosebank from her constituents in "regularly flooded Shrewsbury" and said fossil fuels "belong in the past, not the future".
She urged Fahnbulleh to "reject the oil licence in favour of renewables", adding: "Please don't add further to our climate emergency."
Other Labour MPs expressed their support, including recently departed veterans minister Al Carns, who warned that Britain wouldcontinue to need fossil fuelsfor decades and importing more would be a mistake.
"Refusing to produce it here does nothing on its own to eliminate that demand - it simply increases our reliance on imports which can carry their own environmental cost," he added.
Those representing communities with ties to the oil and gas industry, including Jonathan Brash, the Labour MP for Hartlepool, stressed the benefits of approving Rosebank for British jobs.
Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, Labour MP Bill Esterson, chair of Energy Security and Net Zero Committee, said "the economics of it (Rosebank) are that you should carry on with it" and "there's an element of energy security" by approving it.
Energy minister Michael Shanks told the debate the government would take a "pragmatic approach" to a clean energy transition, stressing it was "not a turn off the taps government, but nor can we justifiably be a drill every last drop government either".
"This government will not make decisions for this country which are not compatible with our climate obligations," he added.
